layers.name: Core
layers.purpose: Core is the package a spec is written against: the fluent language, the model a spec compiles to, and the readers of that model that need no compiler.

layers.name: Model
layers.purpose: Model is the reified spec: the nodes a spec compiles to, and the one thing the checker and the renderers both read.

layers.name: Checking
layers.purpose: Checking evaluates each rule of the model against an extracted codebase: a verdict per rule, its violations, and what the baselines grandfather.

layers.name: Rendering
layers.purpose: Rendering turns the model and a check's results into what people and agents read: the managed block and cards, the diagrams, and the reports.

layers.name: Extraction
layers.purpose: Extraction reads a compilation into a fragment of the codebase model and merges the fragments into the model the checker evaluates against, using the compiler API and nothing else.

layers.name: Analyzers
layers.purpose: Analyzers runs the extractor and the checker inside the C# compiler, over the one project being built, and reports a broken rule as a warning at the offending code, in the editor as it is typed and in the build.

layers.name: SpecAnalyzers
layers.purpose: SpecAnalyzers runs Core's literal checks inside the C# compiler, over a spec project as it is written, and reports a bad string literal as a warning on the literal.

layers.name: SpecCompletion
layers.purpose: SpecCompletion offers the namespaces and types a spec can anchor on inside the editor a spec is written in, reading the same slot markers the spec analyzer reads.

layers.name: Workspace
layers.purpose: Workspace is the Roslyn host: it loads a solution through MSBuild or a build log, hands each compilation to Extraction, and keeps the extraction cache and the baseline files.

layers.name: Host
layers.purpose: Host is the `sliderule` command: the CLI commands, the MCP server, and the spec loading and pipeline behind both.

layers.name: Adapter
layers.purpose: Adapter runs every rule of a spec as an individually named xUnit test in the consumer's own test project.

layers.name: Pack
layers.purpose: Pack is the shared rule pack: canonical .NET rules as an ordinary class library that a spec takes one method at a time.

rules.sentence: The Core layer must not reference the Extraction layer, the Workspace layer, types in `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.*` or types in `Microsoft.Build.*`.
rules.because: Core is the netstandard2.0 reified model both render targets consume; reading a compilation is the work of the two layers above it, and a Microsoft.CodeAnalysis or Microsoft.Build package reference would leak compiler types into Core just as a project reference to either layer would.
rules.fix: Depend on the Codebase model types in Core; keep Microsoft.CodeAnalysis behind SlideRule.Extraction and SlideRule.Roslyn.

rules.sentence: The Extraction layer must not reference the Workspace layer, the Host layer, the Adapter layer, the Pack layer, types in `Microsoft.Build.*` or types in `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.MSBuild.*`.
rules.because: The extractor runs wherever a compilation exists, with no workspace and no build engine behind it, and that holds only while the compiler API is the whole of what it needs. The build already refuses a project reference up to Workspace, Host or Adapter, since each of them depends on this project. What it does not refuse is a package: a reference to Microsoft.Build or to the MSBuild workspace compiles, passes every test, and leaves an assembly that loads only in a process that can also load MSBuild.
rules.fix: Take the fact as data instead. A caller that has a workspace reads what the extractor needs out of it and passes that in; anything that needs MSBuild belongs in SlideRule.Roslyn.

rules.sentence: The Analyzers layer must not reference the Workspace layer, types in `Microsoft.Build.*` or types in `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.MSBuild.*`.
rules.because: The analyzer is loaded by whichever compiler is building the project: csc on the command line, the compiler server, Visual Studio. None of them has a workspace or a build engine to give it, and an assembly that needs either does not load there. The compiler reports that as one warning about the analyzer and carries on without it, so the build goes quiet where it should have gone red.
rules.fix: Take what the analyzer needs from the compilation and the additional files the build hands it; anything that needs a workspace or MSBuild belongs in SlideRule.Roslyn, behind `sliderule check`.

rules.sentence: The Model layer must not reference the Checking layer or the Rendering layer.
rules.because: The Model is the one reified thing this product is built around: a spec compiles to it, and checking and rendering are two independent readers of it. A reference the other way would make the model know about a consumer, and the next render target could no longer be added without touching it.
rules.fix: Keep the dependency one-way: give Model the data, and let Checking or Rendering read it.

rules.sentence: Each of the Model, Checking and Rendering layers must not have circular references with the others.
rules.because: Model, Checking and Rendering are three cuts inside one assembly with one intended direction: a model and two readers of it. A circle among them means a reader has become something the other reader depends on, and the next render target or checker change could no longer land without touching both.
rules.fix: Move what a reader borrows from another reader down to where both can reach it: Model for shared data, a helper namespace for a helper. A reader depends on the model, never on the other reader.

rules.sentence: Each of the Host, Adapter, Pack, Analyzers, SpecAnalyzers and SpecCompletion layers must not reference the others.
rules.because: Host, Adapter, Pack, Analyzers, SpecAnalyzers and SpecCompletion are the six leaves of the project graph: each is a different way to consume Core, and none is a dependency of another. A reference between two leaves would pull one consumer's closure — the CLI's MSBuild and MCP machinery, the adapter's xunit, the pack's canonical rules, an analyzer's compiler host — into a project that ships without it.
rules.fix: Move the shared piece down into Core, or into Extraction or Workspace if it needs Roslyn; a leaf takes what it needs from below, never from a sibling.

rules.sentence: The Pack layer must reference only the Core layer (external packages are not constrained by this rule).
rules.because: A spec project takes the rule pack as a reference of its own, and the whole of what the pack needs is the Arch it composes onto. A reference to the Workspace layer or the CLI would pull MSBuild and the rest of the tool into the closure of every spec project that takes the pack — and nothing in the project graph stops it, because the pack is a leaf and no reference out of it would be circular.
rules.fix: Express the rule in the Core vocabulary the pack already has; anything that needs a workspace belongs in the tool, not in a pack.

rules.sentence: The SpecAnalyzers layer must reference only the Core layer (external packages are not constrained by this rule).
rules.because: The spec analyzer ships inside the contract package, in a directory that holds it and one neighbour, Core, and a compiler resolves an analyzer's dependencies from that directory and nowhere else. A reference to Extraction or to any other project here compiles and passes every test, because the test process can load it, and then fails to load inside the compiler of everyone who references the package. The sibling analyzer project references Extraction and is the obvious thing to copy, and nothing in the project graph stops it, because this project is a leaf.
rules.fix: Take what the analyzer needs from Core, and put a verdict it lacks into Core's validation, where loading a spec reads it too; anything that needs the extractor belongs in SlideRule.Analyzers.

rules.sentence: The SpecCompletion layer must reference only itself (external packages are not constrained by this rule).
rules.because: An editor builds a project's completion providers by reflection, inside handlers that report nothing, so an assembly it cannot load produces no list and no message anywhere. This one ships in the contract package's analyzer directory beside the contract and the spec analyzer, and a reference to either compiles, passes every test and then fails to load in the editor of everyone who references the package, where the only symptom is a list that never appears. Nothing in the project graph stops it, because this project is a leaf.
rules.fix: Mirror the handful of names it needs and hold each copy to its owner with a test that sees both sides; a verdict it lacks belongs in Core's validation, where loading a spec reads it too.

rules.sentence: The Adapter layer must not be referenced by the Core layer, the Extraction layer or the Workspace layer.
rules.because: The adapter rides xunit.v3; a product reference would ship a test framework to every consumer of the referencing package. Host, Pack, Analyzers, SpecAnalyzers and SpecCompletion are the other five leaves, and layering/leaves-independent already holds all six off each other, so this rule names only what sits below the adapter.
rules.fix: Keep the dependency one-way: the adapter consumes Core and Workspace, never the reverse.

rules.sentence: Types in `SlideRule` must belong to `Accessibility`, `Arch`, `Constraint`, `FieldSelection`, `FieldSelectionConstraints`, `IArchitectureSpec`, `IAttributeInfo`, `IMemberInfo`, `IPackageReferenceInfo`, `IParameterInfo`, `IProjectInfo`, `IProjectPropertyInfo`, `IRuleBuilder`, `IScopeBuilder`, `ITypeInfo`, `Layer`, `Lifetime`, `Member`, `MemberKind`, `MemberSelection`, `MemberSelectionAdjectives`, `MemberSelectionConstraints`, `MethodSelection`, `MethodSelectionConstraints`, `MigrationPolicy`, `ProjectSelection`, `ProjectSelectionAdjectives`, `ProjectSelectionConstraints`, `PropertySelection`, `PropertySelectionConstraints`, `Selection`, `SelectionAdjectives`, `SelectionConstraints`, `SpecValidation` or `TypeKind`.
rules.because: The root namespace is the authoring surface. Someone writes `using SlideRule;` and what completion offers from there is, in practice, the whole language they believe exists — so a type that lands in it uninvited is one more thing to read past before finding the verb they wanted, and that cost falls in the first hour with the product. Hiding the rest is free: member resolution on a return type ignores using directives, so a chain keeps flowing through types nobody imports.
rules.fix: Put the type where it belongs — Fluent for an intermediate a chain only passes through, Hosting for a node of the built model, Model/Checking/Rendering/Validation for the machinery behind them. If it really is a type an author spells, add it to this rule's list in the spec and say in review what an author writes it for.

rules.sentence: Types in `SlideRule.Extraction`, except private types, must belong to types named `CodebaseModelBuilder`, `CompilationInput`, `ExtractionInputs`, `FragmentExtractor`, `FragmentMerger`, `ProjectArtifactFacts` or `SiblingProjects`.
rules.because: The root of this assembly is what a host calls to turn compilations into a codebase model: the input it fills in, the extractor, the merger, and the builder that runs both. The fragment records and the passes sit in namespaces behind it so that they stay free to change shape. A type left in the root reads as one more thing a host may call, and the first host to take it up turns the next rearrangement of the extractor's internals into a break in every process that loads it.
rules.fix: Put the type in Fragments if the extractor and the merger exchange it, or in Passes if it is a step of the walk. If a host genuinely calls it, add its name to this rule's list in the spec.

rules.sentence: Types in `SlideRule.Roslyn` must belong to types named `CodebaseExtractor`, `LoadedSolution`, `PathCanonicalizer`, `SolutionDiscovery`, `UserErrorException`, `WorkspaceLoader`, `WorkspaceSession` or `WorkspaceSnapshot`.
rules.because: This assembly travels inside the tool and the xUnit adapter, and its root is the seam those two hosts call, which leaves everything behind it free to be rearranged. A type left sitting in the root reads as part of that seam, and the first host to take it up ties the next rearrangement of the internals to a change in both hosts.
rules.fix: Put the type beside its siblings in Baselines, Caching, Checking, Diagnostics, Files, Hosting, Replay, Sessions or Solutions. If it genuinely belongs on the seam, add it to this rule's list in the spec.

rules.sentence: Types in `SlideRule.Cli` must belong to types named `CliEntry`, `CliErrorMapper`, `CommandEntryPoint` or `CommandFactory`.
rules.because: Namespaces are not API here — this project ships as a tool — so the only thing the root namespace buys is legibility, and that is worth holding. The entry path is the first thing anyone reads to learn how the tool starts, and a root that also holds the verb requests, runners and pipeline stages it dispatches to hides that path among the thirty types it calls.
rules.fix: Put the type beside its siblings in Diff, Mcp, Pipeline, Rendering, Replay, SpecLoading or Verbs. If it is really part of the entry path, add its name to this rule's list in the spec.

rules.sentence: Types in the Core layer named `*Constraint`, except `Constraint`, must reside in `SlideRule.Model.*`.
rules.because: A `*Constraint` is a node of the reified model — what a spec compiles to and what both render targets read back. The checker's dispatch and the sentence renderer each switch over the whole set, so a constraint node declared somewhere else is one they would silently not handle. `Constraint` itself is the public base a spec author names, so it stays in the root namespace with the rest of the authoring surface.
rules.fix: Put the new constraint node in SlideRule.Model beside its siblings, and handle it in ConstraintEvaluator and SentenceRenderer.

rules.sentence: Properties of types derived from `Selection`, types derived from `Constraint`, types derived from `MemberSelection` or types derived from `ProjectSelection` must be get-only.
rules.because: A spec compiles to these nodes and both render targets read them back, so a node is a value: the same spec must render the same sentence and check to the same verdict whoever walks it, and a settable property is the one way a walker could change what the next walker sees. The four roots are the whole reified hierarchy an author can name — a selection, a constraint, the member selection a projection mints, and the project selection the artifact noun mints — and their private-protected constructors mean no assembly outside Core can add a fifth. The BUILDERS are deliberately outside this law and stay mutable: a RuleRegistration accumulates a posture and a constraint across chained calls, which is what makes the stage machine a stage machine.
rules.fix: Take the value in the constructor and expose it `{ get; }`. If a node genuinely has to accumulate, it is a builder, not a node — put it beside RuleRegistration.

rules.sentence: Project `SlideRule` must target only `netstandard2.0`.
rules.because: netstandard2.0 is the one TFM a net48 spec project and the net10 host can both load; Core is the contract every spec references, so its TFM is the product's reach.
rules.fix: Anything needing a newer API belongs in SlideRule.Roslyn or the CLI, never Core.

rules.sentence: Project `SlideRule` must reference no NuGet packages other than private ones, whose `PrivateAssets` is `all` (declared references only; transitive dependencies are not seen).
rules.because: Every consumer's spec csproj takes Core directly; a package Core drags along is imposed on every estate that adopts the tool, and a net48 spec has to resolve it too.
rules.fix: Use what the netstandard2.0 surface already supplies, or put the dependency behind SlideRule.Roslyn or the CLI, where a package reference costs only the tool.

rules.sentence: Projects `SlideRule.Extraction`, `SlideRule.Analyzers`, `SlideRule.SpecAnalyzers` or `SlideRule.SpecCompletion` must target `netstandard2.0`.
rules.because: A compiler loads these four projects: the analyzer package carries Extraction beside the build analyzer, and the contract package carries the spec analyzer and the completion provider. Visual Studio runs its compiler on .NET Framework and the dotnet CLI runs it on .NET, and netstandard2.0 is the one target both of them can load.
rules.fix: Keep netstandard2.0 among the project's target frameworks. An API it lacks belongs in SlideRule.Roslyn or the CLI, which no compiler loads.

rules.sentence: Projects `SlideRule.Extraction`, `SlideRule.Analyzers`, `SlideRule.SpecAnalyzers` or `SlideRule.SpecCompletion` must reference only NuGet packages matching `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis*`, other than private ones, whose `PrivateAssets` is `all` (declared references only; transitive dependencies are not seen).
rules.because: A compiler resolves an analyzer's dependencies from the directory it loaded the analyzer from, and the packages put nothing there but these assemblies and Core. A reference to any other package compiles and passes every test, because the test process can load it, and then fails to load inside the compiler of everyone who installs the package. The compiler's own packages are the exception, because the compiler supplies them itself.
rules.fix: Take what the package supplies from the compiler API or from Core. A dependency that cannot be avoided belongs in SlideRule.Roslyn or the CLI.

rules.sentence: Projects matching `SlideRule*`, except project `SlideRule.Cli`, must not reference NuGet packages matching `ModelContextProtocol*` (declared references only; transitive dependencies are not seen).
rules.because: The package-level form of mcp/tool-types-in-cli: that rule keeps the tool classes in the CLI, and this one keeps their SDK there. A reference from any other project carries the SDK into what that project ships: from Core into every spec project, and from the adapter into every consumer's test project.
rules.fix: Keep MCP code in SlideRule.Cli.Mcp beside the tool classes; only the CLI references the MCP SDK.

rules.sentence: Projects matching `SlideRule*`, except projects `SlideRule.Xunit` or `SlideRule.Tests`, must not reference NuGet packages matching `xunit*` (declared references only; transitive dependencies are not seen).
rules.because: The package-level form of layering/adapter-is-a-leaf: the adapter and this repository's tests are the only projects here that run inside a test process. An xunit reference anywhere else ships a test framework in the tool, the contract or the build analyzer, to consumers who never run a test with it.
rules.fix: Put code that needs the test framework in SlideRule.Xunit, or in the tests if it is a test.

rules.sentence: Packable projects matching `SlideRule*` must lock package restore.
rules.because: CI restores locked; a shipping project without a lock file floats its dependency graph under audit.
rules.fix: Set `RestorePackagesWithLockFile` to true and commit the packages.lock.json the next restore writes; src/Directory.Build.props already carries the policy for everything under it.

rules.sentence: Packable projects matching `SlideRule*` must set `GenerateDocumentationFile` to `true`.
rules.because: A consumer's editor shows a package's doc comments only from the XML file packed beside its assembly, and the compiler checks the doc comments only while it writes that file. A shipping project that stops generating it ships an API with no documentation, and a doc comment that names a type which no longer exists then builds green.
rules.fix: Set `GenerateDocumentationFile` to true. src/Directory.Build.props already sets it for every project under src/.

rules.sentence: Projects matching `SlideRule*`, except projects `SlideRule`, `SlideRule.Analyzers`, `SlideRule.Xunit` or `SlideRule.Cli`, must not be packable.
rules.because: Only the packages named in this rule ship, and the SDK packs by default, so a project that stays silent about it is one release-pipeline accident away from publishing this repository's internals under a name nobody reviewed.
rules.fix: Set `IsPackable` to false in the project file. A project that genuinely should ship joins the names in this rule's subject in the same change.

rules.sentence: Singleton-registered types in `SlideRule.*` must not inject scoped-registered types or transient-registered types.
rules.because: The MCP server is one long-lived process wired all-singleton by design (IEnvironment, WorkspaceSession, SessionFragmentStore, SpecModelCache, SpecResolutionCache, ISolutionSource); a scoped or transient service injected into a singleton is captured for the whole process and silently shared across every tool call.
rules.fix: Keep singletons depending only on singletons; resolve any scoped or transient work per call inside an IServiceScopeFactory scope instead of injecting it into the singleton.

rules.sentence: Types in the Host layer, except types named `McpServerCommand` or `GlobalCallToolFilter`, must not use `IServiceProvider.GetService()`, `ServiceProviderServiceExtensions.GetService()` or `ServiceProviderServiceExtensions.GetRequiredService()`.
rules.because: Resolving services from IServiceProvider at call sites hides a type's real dependencies; declare them as constructor parameters.
rules.fix: Take the dependency in the constructor; McpServerCommand's composition root and GlobalCallToolFilter's request context are the only sanctioned resolve sites.

rules.sentence: Types in `SlideRule.*` must not use `ServiceCollectionContainerBuilderExtensions.BuildServiceProvider()`.
rules.because: Calling BuildServiceProvider while configuring services builds a second container with its own singletons, a duplicate-instance trap.
rules.fix: Register the dependency and let the host build the provider once; inject what you need.

rules.sentence: The Host layer must not use `Console.Out`, `Console.Write()` or `Console.WriteLine()`.
rules.because: Stdout is a protocol channel here — the MCP server speaks JSON-RPC over it and CLI output flows through System.CommandLine's console — so a direct Console write corrupts the wire and is invisible to the in-process tests.
rules.fix: Write CLI output through the command's InvocationConfiguration console; route server diagnostics to the logger or Console.Error.

rules.sentence: `[McpServerTool]`-attributed methods of types in `SlideRule.*` must accept a parameter of type `CancellationToken`.
rules.because: Tool calls run inside one long-lived server process; a tool method without a CancellationToken cannot honor a client cancel and holds the idle watchdog open.
rules.fix: Add a trailing CancellationToken parameter (default it) and flow it into the runner.

rules.sentence: Types in `SlideRule.Cli.Mcp.Tools.*` must be attributed with `[McpServerToolType]`.
rules.because: Tool discovery is the attribute walk: WithCoercingTools registers the [McpServerTool] methods of [McpServerToolType]-annotated classes, so a tool class without the type attribute compiles, registers nothing, and its tools silently vanish from the server.
rules.fix: Put [McpServerToolType] on the tool class, and keep tool classes in SlideRule.Cli.Mcp.Tools.

rules.sentence: Types attributed with `[McpServerToolType]` must reside in project `SlideRule.Cli`.
rules.because: The converse of mcp/tool-types-attributed: that rule keeps every type in the tools namespace attributed, and this one keeps every attributed type in the CLI. The ModelContextProtocol SDK is the CLI's package reference alone, so a tool class declared in Core or Roslyn would drag the SDK into that package's closure — Core's rides into every spec project that references the contract library.
rules.fix: Move the tool class into SlideRule.Cli.Mcp.Tools beside ArchTools; only the CLI references the MCP SDK.

rules.sentence: Types in the Host, Workspace or Extraction layers, except types named `ServerShutdown`, must not use `Task.Wait()`, `Task<TResult>.Result`, `ValueTask<TResult>.Result`, `TaskAwaiter.GetResult()`, `TaskAwaiter<TResult>.GetResult()`, `ValueTaskAwaiter.GetResult()` or `ValueTaskAwaiter<TResult>.GetResult()`.
rules.because: The CLI and the two layers under it are one long-lived MCP server as often as they are a one-shot command, and a blocking wait there costs twice: it holds a thread-pool thread for as long as the child process or workspace load it waits on, and it drops the CancellationToken the tool call was handed, so a client cancel leaves a zombie running the timeout out instead. ServerShutdown is the one sanctioned block — a bounded drain at process exit, with nothing left to starve.
rules.fix: Await the task and flow the CancellationToken. Where a call chain genuinely cannot be async — the MSBuild registration path is JIT-quarantined behind a synchronous seam — wait on the resource itself, a process handle rather than a Task.

rules.sentence: Types in the Host layer, except types named `SpecLoadContext`, must not use `AssemblyLoadContext.LoadFromAssemblyPath()`.
rules.because: A host that loads an assembly from its path pins that file for as long as the host lives, and this host lives for a whole session: the model roots the spec's Types, so the collectible context never collects and the operating system never releases the build output. Every rebuild of what was loaded then fails, and the only cure is killing the server — which for a stdio server is terminal, because the client never reconnects one, so the session's architecture queries go dead with no error anywhere. SpecLoadContext is the single sanctioned caller: it reads bytes, and reaches for the loader only when the file is already gone.
rules.fix: Read the assembly's bytes and load from the stream, the way LoadWithoutLocking does in the exemplar; never hand a path to the loader from the CLI.

rules.sentence: Types in the Host layer, except types named `McpServerCommand`, must not construct types named `WorkspaceSession`, `SessionFragmentStore`, `SpecModelCache` or `SpecResolutionCache`.
rules.because: The warm server holds exactly one of each piece of session state for its lifetime — the workspace session, the fragment store, and the two spec caches that hang off the same load. A second construction forks the reconcile state and the caches silently diverge: the fork answers from an empty cache while the original keeps ratcheting, so the cost the cache exists to remove comes back and nothing reports it.
rules.fix: Resolve them from DI; only McpServerCommand's composition root constructs them.

rules.sentence: Types in `SlideRule.Cli.Mcp.Infrastructure.*`, except types named `SystemEnvironment`, must not use `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable()`, `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariables()`, `Environment.ExpandEnvironmentVariables()` or `Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable()`.
rules.because: A single IEnvironment seam keeps the MCP pipeline testable without mutating real process state: a test sets a variable on the fake, never on the process.
rules.fix: Inject IEnvironment and read through GetVariable; SystemEnvironment alone reads the real process environment.

rules.sentence: Types in `SlideRule.*` must not use `MSBuildLocator.QueryVisualStudioInstances()`.
rules.because: On .NET hosts QueryVisualStudioInstances returns no VS Setup instances, so code consulting it silently picks the wrong MSBuild; the sanctioned path is vswhere (VsWhereLocator). The quarantine's dragons warn this in prose — this rule is the teeth.
rules.fix: Go through MsBuildBootstrap / VsWhereLocator; never query the Locator for instances.

rules.sentence: The Adapter layer must throw only `FileNotFoundException` or `InvalidOperationException`.
rules.because: The adapter runs inside consumers' test processes; its own failures must surface as the two documented setup errors, not as arbitrary exception noise beside the rule results.
rules.fix: Route new failure modes through FileNotFoundException (missing solution) or InvalidOperationException (bad configuration).

rules.sentence: Properties of types in the Adapter layer named `ArchRuleTests` must be overridable.
rules.because: Every property of ArchRuleTests is a hook a consumer's test class overrides: SolutionPath always, ExcludeProjectName and AllowWorkspaceDiagnostics when their defaults do not fit. A property that cannot be overridden is a setting no consumer can change.
rules.fix: Declare the property abstract or virtual. A value the adapter computes for itself belongs in a private member.

rules.sentence: Properties of types in the Adapter layer named `ArchRuleTests` must be protected.
rules.because: A consumer overrides each hook as `protected override`, the shape the adapter's README shows, and an override keeps the access of the member it overrides. A hook declared public breaks that override with CS0507, and a private protected one cannot be overridden outside the adapter's assembly.
rules.fix: Declare the hook protected.

rules.sentence: The Core or Extraction layers must not reference `File`, `Directory`, `Environment`, `Console`, `Process`, `ProcessStartInfo` or `Random`.
rules.because: The analyzer package ships Core and Extraction in the directory the compiler loads the analyzer from, and the contract package ships a second Core copy beside its own analyzer, so both of these run inside csc: there is no console, the working directory belongs to whoever started the build, and one compiler server outlives many builds. RS1035 holds the analyzer projects to this list and cannot see the assemblies beside them.
rules.fix: Take the value as a parameter, or through a host seam the CLI fills in; an assembly the compiler loads reads only what the compilation hands it.

rules.sentence: The Core or Extraction layers must not use `Path.GetTempPath()`, `Assembly.Load()`, `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture` or `CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture`.
rules.because: These four reach the same ambient world through types both layers otherwise use correctly — Path for path arithmetic, CultureInfo for the invariant culture, Assembly for reflection-only discovery — so the ban is member-level, where banning the types would red on code that is right.
rules.fix: Take the directory as a parameter, compare with InvariantCulture or Ordinal, and let the runtime resolve dependencies from the directory it loaded this assembly from.

rules.sentence: Types in the Core, Extraction, Analyzers, SpecAnalyzers, SpecCompletion, Workspace, Host, Adapter or Pack layers, except types named `ArchChecker`, `ArchRuleTests`, `BuildTierAnalyzer`, `CommandEntryPoint`, `IdleTimeoutWatchdog`, `ParentProcessWatcher`, `ServerShutdown`, `SpecLiteralAnalyzer` or `VsWhereLocator`, must not swallow `Exception`.
rules.because: A broad catch that holds the failure and continues holds the ones nobody thought about — a cancellation, an out-of-memory, the bug introduced two lines up — and hands the caller a wrong answer that reads like a right one. Two shapes are not that, and this rule passes both: a `when` filter is where a handler writes down what it is actually for, so everything else keeps travelling (`catch (Exception ex) when (ex is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)`); and a clause that ends in a `throw` — cleanup-and-rethrow, or translate-and-throw — suppresses nothing at all. The sanctioned handlers are exempt by type name rather than by site, the same granularity a baseline would give, stated in the spec instead of recorded in a file.
rules.fix: Rethrow after the cleanup, translate to a type that names the failure, or add a `when` filter naming the exceptions this handler is for. A handler that genuinely has to hold everything and continue, like a process boundary or a background loop, goes on the spec's sanctioned list instead.

rules.sentence: The Core, Extraction, Analyzers, SpecAnalyzers, SpecCompletion, Workspace, Host, Adapter or Pack layers must not throw `Exception`, `SystemException` or `ApplicationException`.
rules.because: A bare BCL exception type says only that something went wrong. A caller cannot filter on it, so throwing one forces every handler above into the swallowed broad catch `exceptions/no-swallowed-broad-catches` exists to prevent, and leaves a message string as the only thing left to match on. Nothing here throws one today; this rule is what stops the first one arriving unnoticed.
rules.fix: Throw a type that names the failure — one of this repo's own error types, or the closest BCL type such as InvalidOperationException or IOException — so a handler can filter on it.

rules.sentence: Static fields of authored types in the Core, Extraction, Analyzers, SpecAnalyzers, SpecCompletion, Workspace, Host, Adapter or Pack layers, except `s_inFlightCount`, `s_lastActivityTicks`, `s_drainWaiter` or `s_timestampProvider` fields of types named `IdleTimeoutWatchdog`, `s_hasExited` fields of types named `ServerShutdown`, `_loadCount` fields of types named `WorkspaceLoader` or `s_run` fields of types named `ArchRuleTests`, must be readonly.
rules.because: A writable static is process-wide state in a library a long-lived MCP server calls concurrently and every spec project links: whoever wrote to it last decides what the next caller reads, and nothing in the type system says so. A const counts as readonly here — it is readonly's superset — so the law asks for the weakest thing that closes the hole.
rules.fix: Make it `readonly` or `const`. If it has to be written (an Interlocked location, a lock-guarded one-shot or a test seam), add it to this rule's `Except` in the spec, with its family in the comment on the rule, and say in review which one.

rules.sentence: Methods returning `Task`, `Task<TResult>`, `ValueTask` or `ValueTask<TResult>` declared in authored types in the Core, Extraction, Analyzers, SpecAnalyzers, SpecCompletion, Workspace, Host, Adapter or Pack layers, except `Rule_Holds` or `Workspace_LoadedCompletely` methods of types named `ArchRuleTests` or `WhenAllCallsComplete` methods of types named `IdleTimeoutWatchdog`, must be named `*Async`.
rules.because: House convention held repo-wide: an agent grepping *Async sees every await point. The three exceptions are deliberate, not drift: Rule_Holds and Workspace_LoadedCompletely are the adapter's test methods, whose names a consumer reads in every test run, and WhenAllCallsComplete takes its name from Task.WhenAll, the combinator it mirrors.
rules.fix: Name Task-returning methods with the Async suffix.

rules.sentence: Interfaces in `SlideRule.*` must be named `I*`.
rules.because: Nearly every seam here is an interface — ISolutionSource, IEnvironment, IArchitectureSpec — and the `I` prefix is what lets a reader or an agent tell the port from its implementation at a glance, and what makes `I*` a reliable grep for the seams. A convention that holds for most types tells you nothing; this one is total.
rules.fix: Give the interface the `I` prefix.

rules.sentence: Types in the Workspace layer in `SlideRule.Roslyn.MsBuild.*`, except types named `MsBuildBootstrap`, must be referenced only by types in the Workspace layer in `SlideRule.Roslyn.MsBuild.*` or types named `MsBuildBootstrap`.
rules.because: Fragile host bootstrap; contain it behind MsBuildBootstrap.
rules.fix: use types named `MsBuildBootstrap`

scope.dragons: We pick a VS 16/17 via vswhere and hand it to the out-of-process BuildHost through VSINSTALLDIR/VSCMD_VER=99.0. That preference is caution about a moving target, not a live workaround: the TypeInitializationException (XMakeElements) on legacy-namespace projects came from an early VS 18 preview and does not reproduce on VS 18.6. Where no 16/17 is installed, the highest available is taken and MsBuildBootstrap.LastSelection says so — the CLI prints it beside any workspace-load diagnostic, and SLIDERULE_VS_INSTALL_PATH overrides the choice. Do NOT switch to MSBuildLocator.QueryVisualStudioInstances — on .NET it returns no VS Setup instances.

rules.because: Every reader in Core reaches into Model and every renderer assembles its fragments, so nothing here can be fenced; the hazard is an edit that reads as tidying.

scope.dragons: Every node here declares the prose fragment the renderers assemble into its sentence, and the fragments are position-blind: one phrase serves subject and reference position, so a fragment never closes its own parenthetical — the closing comma belongs to the junction (SentenceRenderer.EndsOpen and CloseBefore). A strict verb renders its strictness by the absence of the external-packages caveat; do not add one. A changed fragment moves its pin in the same commit.
